title: 3.4.16 Lab: Rewrite 3 Named Functions as Arrows
description: Convert three function declarations into one-line arrow expressions and confirm each still behaves the same. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the three declarations
steps.instructions: Define three separate function declarations, each with a different job: for example one that returns a number, one that returns a true/false answer, and one that returns a string. Use the function name() {} form.

steps.title: Convert each to an arrow
steps.instructions: Rewrite each declaration as a const assigned a one-line arrow function, using implicit return. Keep the same parameters and the same returned value as the declaration it replaces.

steps.title: Call all three and log results
steps.instructions: Call each of the three arrows with sample arguments and log the results with console.log. Check each result is what the original declaration would have returned.

requirements.title: Three arrow functions
requirements.description: At least three const variables are assigned arrow functions

requirements.title: Implicit return used
requirements.description: An arrow body is a bare expression with no opening brace
